sections.content:
X's dots:
- TL: frame corners (38,8),(38,10),(40,8),(40,10), center (39,9) has 'O' (X's arm passes through the center!). So X's dot TL center = (39,9).
- TR: frame (35,26),(35,28),(37,26),(37,28) → center (36,27) has 'b'?? Wait, row 36 "BbBcbcBB": c is at 26? Columns: c0=23: index 0:B,1:b,2:B,3:c,4:b,5:c,6:B → c is at 26, b at 27, c at 28. So TR dot center (36,27) has a b core! But wait, that's the same position as the blue dot's top (36,27)! The blue top dot's core is (36,27), and X's TR dot is also (36,27)?? They overlap!
Hmm, interesting. So the X's TR dot = (36,27) = the blue's top dot. The dots are shared between objects!
- BL: frame (56,8),(56,10),(58,8),(58,10) → center (57,9) has O. X's BL dot = (57,9).
- BR: frame (59,26),(59,28),(61,26),(61,28) → center (60,27) has b core = blue's bottom dot. Shared!
So the dots:
- (3,21): dark red (diamond)
- (9,27): dark red
- (12,12): dark red
- (39,9): orange (X)
- (36,27): shared (X TR + blue top)
- (57,9): orange (X)
- (60,27): shared (X BR + blue bottom)
- (48,15): blue left
- (48,33): blue right
Total 9 dots. Each object must visit its own dots:
- Diamond: (3,21) [current position], (9,27), (12,12)
- X: (39,9), (36,27), (57,9), (60,27)
- Blue: (36,27), (60,27), (48,15), (48,33)
Current positions: diamond (3,21), X (48,18), blue (48,24).
Movement: step 3, probably 4-directional, no obstacles (open board).
Check reachability (row, col ≡ start mod 3):
- Diamond from (3,21): (9,27): 9-3=6✓, 27-21=6✓. (12,12): 9✓, -9✓.
- X from (48,18): (39,9): 9✓,9✓. (36,27): 12✓,9✓. (57,9): 9✓,9✓. (60,27): 12✓,9✓.
- Blue from (48,24): (36,27): 12✓,3✓. (60,27): 12✓,3✓. (48,15): 9✓. (48,33): 9✓.
All reachable.
Now, how is a dot "collected"? Probably when the object's center lands on the dot. The diamond is currently at (3,21), which is a dot — has it been collected? In the image, the dot at (3,21) is still shown as gray. Maybe it gets collected when you leave, or maybe it's already collected and just remains displayed. Uncertain. Let's test: move the diamond to (9,27) and see if the dot at (3,21) disappears / whether the dot at (9,27) changes.
Actually, wait — maybe the dots are collected when the object's arm passes over them, or when the center is on top of them. The simplest test: move the diamond to (9,27) (2 DOWN + 2 RIGHT = 4 actions), then observe.
But first, which object is "active"? The active object is the one that moves with arrow keys. Currently the blue cross moved (I moved it). SPACE switches the active object. The active one is probably highlighted (brighter). In the image, the blue cross looks bright blue; the X is orange; the diamond is dark red.
Plan: first test the collection mechanic with the diamond? The diamond is at (3,21), which is its dot. If the dot at (3,21) is still shown, then collection may require landing on the dot (already achieved) — but the level isn't complete, so maybe collection only happens when you land on a dot from a different position, or the dot is only collected when visited and the level completes when all dots are collected.
Let's do a probe: switch to the diamond (SPACE until the diamond is active), move to (9,27), and observe the dot state.
How do I know which object is active? Probably the active one is brighter / has a white center W. The blue cross has a W center. The X's center: check if there's a W at (48,18)? The X's center is the 'O' intersection. The diamond's center? Let's check the W pixels: earlier the only W was (48,24) — the blue center. So the active object has a W center marker! The X's center (48,18) currently has no W (the X isn't active). The diamond's center (3,21) also has no W.
So SPACE cycles the active object; the active one shows a W at its center.
Plan:
1. SPACE → activate X or diamond (check which one).
2. Move the diamond to (9,27), observe whether the dot at (3,21) is collected (disappears) or whether the dot at (9,27) is collected.
Then continue the tour.
Let's execute: press SPACE, check the W position to identify the active object.
